title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues §1.17 and opens Chapter 2 of the May 1966 letter to Tate, in which Grothendieck sets out the programme of crystals and crystalline cohomology.

(1) End of 1.17: a fallback if the first construction fails.
- The plan is to define cohomology of the 'cristallogène' site, which is the early, pre-divided-power version of the crystalline site. Its objects are thickenings U→T over R, ringed by O_C.
- Suppose the derived functors of the global-sections or direct-image functor, computed in the category of all O_C-modules, do not give de Rham cohomology.
- Then one could instead derive these functors inside the category of quasi-coherent O_C-modules only, i.e. inside the category of crystals of modules.
- In modern terms: replace sheaf cohomology on the ringed site by derived functors in the category of quasi-coherent crystals. One could also compare RΓ computed in D(O_C-Mod) with RΓ computed in D(Crys).
- A marginal note on the previous page records the later diagnosis. The naive site works in characteristic 0 but not in characteristic p>0, because divided powers have not been introduced.

(2) Chapter 2, 'De Rham cohomology is a crystal'.
- Grothendieck states this as a conjecture or 'pious wish'.
- The precise claim: for a proper smooth f: X→S, the relative de Rham cohomology R^i f_*(Ω•_{X/S}), or better the complex Rf_*(Ω•_{X/S}), is the value on S of a crystal or complex of crystals. Its Gauss–Manin connection would be the stratification coming from the crystal structure.

Two pieces of evidence are given on this page.
- (a) Washnitzer–Monsky cohomology. Grothendieck names two defects.
  - Their invariants are local. A global invariant is obtained only in dimension 1.
  - They are vector spaces over Frac(W), not modules over W. They are therefore 'modulo isogeny', since the invariance proof uses denominators.
  - Hence the title may have to read 'De Rham cohomology defines an isocrystal'. This is the handwritten addition '(et "est" par "définit")'.
  - A good cohomology theory of crystals would still be possible. For proper smooth morphisms and the unit crystal it would agree with de Rham cohomology up to isogeny.
  - The decisive test is whether it works only in characteristic 0 or in all characteristics.
- (b) Gauss–Manin. Grothendieck has checked that for every smooth f: X→S there is a canonical ('absolue') connection on the R^i f_* of relative de Rham cohomology. More precisely, it lives on the complex Rf_*Ω•_{X/S} as an object of D(O_S); this continues on the next page.
errors: The fallback of deriving 'in the category of crystals of modules' presupposes that this category is abelian with enough injectives. The next page states outright that crystals of modules form an abelian category. This holds for cokernels. Kernels are not in general crystals: the transition maps u^*E_T → E_{T'} along non-flat maps between thickenings do not commute with kernels. Later treatments (Berthelot, Berthelot–Ogus) work instead with all O-modules on the crystalline site and with quasi-coherent crystals as a full subcategory. So the fallback is not well-posed as stated, without flatness hypotheses or a different ambient category.

The cristallogène site without divided powers does not give de Rham cohomology in characteristic p. Grothendieck himself flags this in the later marginal note on the previous page. The page's optimism that the main obstacle is isogeny is therefore misplaced: the real fix (divided powers) is integral, and the isogeny issue is separate. In particular, rigid or Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology is needed for non-proper varieties.

ideas.what: Coining of the term 'isocristal': de Rham cohomology might only define a crystal up to isogeny
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (the term); developed by Berthelot, Ogus, and Katz (Dieudonné–Manin classification)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Tate 1966 (circulated, widely cited); Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', Dix exposés (1968)

ideas.what: Conjecture that relative de Rham cohomology of a proper smooth morphism underlies a crystal, with Gauss–Manin as the crystalline stratification
ideas.modern_name: crystalline nature of de Rham cohomology / base-change and comparison theorem (Berthelot)
ideas.where_published: Dix exposés (Crystals and de Rham cohomology), letter to Tate

ideas.what: Critique of Washnitzer–Monsky: only local invariants, global only in dimension 1, and only over Frac(W)
Deriving functors in the category of quasi-coherent crystals rather than all modules on the site
ideas.modern_name: derived category of crystals vs derived category of O_crys-modules
ideas.usually_credited_to: later work (Berthelot–Ogus; modern derived crystals, Drinfeld, Bhatt–Lurie)

ideas.what: Gauss–Manin connection for any smooth morphism, on Rf_*Ω•_{X/S} in D(O_S)

missed.claim: Grothendieck suggests replacing derived functors on all O_C-modules by derived functors in the category of crystals. The comparison of these two derived categories, and when the latter is even defined, was not systematically taken up in the 1970s. It reappears only in modern derived/prismatic contexts.
missed.quote: de prendre des foncteurs dérivés dans la catégorie des seuls Modules quasi-cohérents sur le site cristallogène, i.e. dans la catégorie des cristaux de modules.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor precursor of the question of whether crystalline (or prismatic) cohomology can be computed purely inside crystals. Modern work (e.g. derived crystals, the 'D(Crys)' comparison) addresses it, so it is mostly of historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known 1966 Tate letter, the birth of crystals and of the word 'isocristal'. Its content is widely cited and was developed in the Dix exposés and by Berthelot. The only less-known detail is the fallback of deriving within the category of crystals, which is minor and partly ill-posed.
transcription_corrections: The handwritten insertion after 'isocristal' reads '(et "est" par "définit")'. It belongs inline after the closing quote of "isocris-tal".
'voeux pieux' is as typed (sic, for 'voeu pieux').
In b), the handwritten insertion '(absolue)' sits above 'sur les'. The X in 'f:X→S' is overwritten by hand.
